title: OpenAI’s new countersuit accuses Apple of ‘unlawfully pressuring vendors’
contentZh:
In Brief
Posted:


9:46 AM PST · November 28, 2026



Image Credits:Andrej Sokolow/picture alliance / Getty Images



		
							
											
									
					
		
	





After Apple sued OpenAI this summer over allegations that the AI company had stolen trade secrets, OpenAI has fired back with a countersuit of its own.

According to Bloomberg, the new suit claims that as OpenAI prepared to enter the hardware market, Apple responded by “by unlawfully pressuring vendors not to work with OpenAI and using expansive employment restraints to limit OpenAI’s access to talented engineers.” 







The suit also accuses Apple of stealing OpenAI’s trade secrets.

Apple told the Financial Times that the countersuit is “a transparent attempt to distract from the substance of Apple’s lawsuit, in which OpenAI has already been ordered to stop using Apple’s confidential information.”

Apple previously alleged that OpenAI leaders, including Chief Hardware Officer Tang Tan, asked candidates to bring Apple hardware components to their job interviews and coached them on how to evade security procedures. OpenAI responded that it has “no interest in other companies’ trade secrets.” 

The dueling lawsuits mark a dramatic souring of the relationship between two companies that in 2024 partnered to integrate OpenAI’s ChatGPT with Apple’s Siri.
